subject: Hosted evaluation decision matrix + demo follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Timmons <alex@storix.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Oct 2025 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted evaluation decision matrix + demo follow-up

Alex — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight decision matrix to help Storix pick a path forward (hosted vs dedicated vs private). I wanted to capture the items we discussed and next steps so we can keep momentum.

Top-level recap:
- Primary goal: real-time summarization feature in the Storix agent (avg prompt ~450 tokens, expected peak concurrent sessions 75–100).
- Hard constraints: P95 latency target <= 400ms for short responses; data residency requirement in US; SOC 2 level security baseline.
- Success signal: end-to-end p95 under 600ms in pilot + < $0.002/token for inference cost target at scale.

Decision matrix (short):
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding, managed scaling, streaming support. Pros: quick sandbox, minimal infra. Cons: shared tenancy (but logical separation), rate caps may require reserved capacity for predictable throughput.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool; lower per-token cost at sustained traffic, SLA-backed. Pros: predictable latency, easier large-batch throughput. Cons: longer lead time to provision and demo.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full data control and compliance. Pros: meets strict regulatory needs. Cons: higher ops cost, slower ramp for trials.

Requested info from Storix to recommend final path:
1) Typical and peak concurrent sessions (you said ~80 peak — please confirm).
2) Example payload sizes (tokens in + tokens expected out).
3) Regulatory constraints beyond SOC 2 (any FedRAMP, HIPAA specifics?).
4) Whether you need a private VPC for the pilot or if a hosted evaluation in a US region is acceptable for the initial 4‑week pilot.

Next steps I propose:
- You send a short traffic profile CSV (I attached a template) — we’ll map to endpoints and ratecap recommendations.
- Redwood will stand up a hosted eval endpoint for 30 days with conservative ratecaps for you to exercise. If you need guaranteed throughput during the pilot we can scope a temporary Dedicated reservation.
- Technical sync w/ our infra lead (Sean) next week to walk ratecap and prefix caching details.

Attachments: storix-eval-traffic.csv (template), Redwood hosted quickstart checklist (PDF).

If that looks right I can schedule the tech sync — what times next Tue/Wed look good?

Best,
Jordan
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Timmons <alex@storix.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@storix.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Oct 2025 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation decision matrix + demo follow-up

Jordan — thanks, that layout is super helpful. A few clarifications from our side: we confirmed the 80 peak sessions (could spike to ~120 for short windows). Average request size is ~420 tokens in, ~160 tokens out. We do have a HIPAA scope for the agent workflows, but the initial pilot can run under our internal QA data (non-PHI) — HIPAA will be required for production.

For the pilot we prefer the hosted evaluation in a US region if we can get:
- dedicated trial endpoints (so we don’t contend with other customers), and
- a soft ratecap of ~250 requests/min per endpoint to start.

We uploaded the traffic CSV to the folder you shared; let me know if the format is OK. Happy to take the tech sync Wed after 11am ET.

— Alex
CTO, Storix
alex@storix.ai
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Timmons <alex@storix.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation decision matrix + demo follow-up

Alex — perfect, thanks for the details and the CSV. I reviewed the brief and we can map a hosted evaluation configuration that meets your pilot asks. Quick answers:

- Dedicated trial endpoints: we can provision a temporary reserved tenant for the 30-day pilot to avoid noisy neighbor issues (this is commonly used for pilots with predictable concurrency).
- Ratecap: 250 req/min per endpoint is feasible as a soft cap; we’ll recommend two endpoints to distribute traffic and hit your p95 latency targets.
- HIPAA: hosted pilot with non-PHI data is fine. For production HIPAA we’ll move to Private deployment or a HIPAA-enabled Dedicated agreement — we’ll route you to our Compliance team for the paperwork once pilot metrics look good.

Sean — can you confirm the quickstart checklist items we should hand to Storix (routing, API keys, prefix caching, streaming config)? I added the checklist PDF to attachments.

Alex — I scheduled the tech sync for Wed 20 Oct, 11:30am ET / 8:30am PT and sent a calendar invite. Agenda: mapping traffic profile to endpoints, ratecap tuning, KV cache prefix suggestions, and a short live test plan. If we confirm the trial reserved tenant, I’ll spin up the hosted trial later that day.

Action items:
- Alex: confirm acceptance of the temporary reserved tenant for pilot (yes/no).
- Jordan: provision trial tenant once confirmed and send endpoint credentials.
- Sean: share quickstart runbook snippet and confirm streaming/kv cache defaults.

Thanks —
Jordan
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Alex Timmons <alex@storix.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Hosted evaluation decision matrix + demo follow-up

Adding the infra notes here — Jordan, Alex:

Quickstart runbook excerpt (high level):
1) Endpoints: we’ll expose two hosted endpoints in us-east-1 (streaming enabled). Endpoint A tuned for short/low-latency (prompt <= 600 tokens), Endpoint B tuned for batch/longer responses.
2) Ratecaps: start with 250 req/min per endpoint, soft enforcement; increase to 375 req/min for Endpoint A if prefix caching lowers compute.
3) KV/prefix caching: enable prefix cache for repeated context; use a 6-hour TTL for the pilot. This reduces per-token compute significantly for repeated prompts.
4) Auth & keys: Redwood will issue scoped API keys for the tenant; rotateable via console.
5) Telemetry: we’ll enable token-level latency sampling and forward a short trace to your Sentry instance if you want request-level debugging.

Attachments referenced: redwood-hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf (procedure), storix-eval-traffic.csv (template).

If Storix confirms the temporary reserved tenant I’ll coordinate provisioning and share the endpoint URLs + sample curl commands.

— Sean
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
